result: Per-input cost profile of 31 f32 + 31 f64 unary and 10 binary libm functions vs glibc: glibc max <= 1025 instructions (except f64 fmod/remainder), Liella has 1e5-5e5-instruction bands on 20-80% of inputs of lgamma/tgamma/Bessel (f32 and f64), erfcf 22%, hypot 98% at ~3.7k; ranked bands in handoff/LIBM-TAIL-PROBE.md

gate.affected: not run (measurement tool + report; clippy and static green)

rulings.item: RETHINK stories for lgammaf/tgammaf (tiny and large |x|), Bessel j0f..y1f (large |x|, tiny x), erfcf/erf tiny and subnormal x, f64 hypot (every input ~3.7k)
rulings.recommendation: one RETHINK story per family in score order; brief files not written in this run

informational: exhaustive f32 done for 24 unary functions; lgammaf tgammaf j0f j1f y0f y1f erfcf sampled per input (1 in 1024) because an exhaustive Liella run projects to ~30 h each
rdpmc traps on the Zen 1 build VM (~35 us per counter read)
Liella ld.so has no library search, so Liella was measured statically linked (liella-cc), as cbench does
glibc tail: f64 fmod/remainder with large exponent gaps, 4% of the sample over 2000 (max 3082)
paths named by exported entry; multi-precision fallback inside math::special inferred from cost, not traced
improvement: rdpmc traps on the build VMs: per-input instruction counting needs batching; a bare-metal or rdpmc-passthrough host would make exhaustive per-input runs feasible
next_step: RETHINK lgamma/tgamma tiny-|x| band (41.8% of f32 inputs at ~4e5 instructions), then Bessel large-|x|; re-run validation/libm_tail/suite.sh after each fix
